# CLAIMs with `tags` `agency`

*Topics — What a work is about. Nucleation holds whatever reading the owner files here, whether or not an Anthology of the SOTA topic could also hold it; instruction for ML practice belongs to the anthology (ADR-048). The words are seeded from the clusters the reading-time triage of 2026-09-25 found, and grow by decision.*

**Agency** — what it is to be an agent — goals, action, control and the capacity to act — in organisms, collectives or machines. An agent is not thereby an individual, a self or a person (ADR-024); how an agent's behaviour is integrated is behavioral-integration, and governing oneself by one's own standards is self-governance (group: philosophy).

| [CLAIM-349](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-349.md) v6 | An organization's access to a signal, the signal's authority over action, and action on it are separable, and adaptive regulation keeps the first while making the second conditional on evidence; overcontrol, which buys freedom from harmful acts by cutting access or making inhibition unconditional, is a maladaptive regime and not more control, so flexibility is a context-sensitive property of maintained influence relations, not of how much is inhibited | The owner's idea, U42 of the exchange of 2026-10-17, on A41's line that an organization "could become extremely resistant to internal changes while losing its capacity to learn, correct errors, or act at all": "useful connections to the ACT and DBT frameworks here, which provide us with accounts/ontologies of maladaption and productive flexibility". | [CLAIM-351](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-351.md) | A zero aggregate gradient does not show that the demands it aggregates are reconciled: with positive weights it holds both when every demand's own gradient vanishes and when nonzero gradients cancel, and in the second case no update improves them all to first order; even the first is only joint first-order stationarity, which a demand's maximum or saddle also has | A33 §5 of the exchange of 2026-10-17: "Zero aggregate gradient does not imply absence of frustrated demands." | [CLAIM-354](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-354.md) v2 | Freedom of will and autonomy come in degrees along several dimensions, among them viable reachability, control cost, robustness to disturbance, governance reconfigurability, revisability and motivational integration, and agents compare by inclusion of what they can viably reach under matched conditions: a partial order with incomparable pairs, not a scalar, and a gradient only of a declared measure | The owner's, U9 of the exchange of 2026-10-17: "controllability of a system isn't binary, and neither is sensitivity to perturbation", so can the account speak of "gradations (perhaps even gradients/spectra?) of freedom of will/autonomy". | [CLAIM-357](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-357.md) v5 | The frustration residual and governance regret separate structural infeasibility, realized violation and minimax suboptimality, and identify none of them as thwarting: a positive residual says no admissible update meets every declared requirement, a positive regret only that the actual update's worst residual exceeds the best achievable, which can hold while every requirement is met, and actual violation needs regret above the negative residual; aggregate performance does not tell infeasibility from realized violation, and the multipliers that certify infeasibility need not be the weights governance assigns | A34 §4 and A35 §3.3 of the exchange of 2026-10-17, restated at A39 §2C and A40 §3.4, from A33's "irreducible conflict" and "manufactured frustration". | [CLAIM-359](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-359.md) v2 | A self-governing organization's robustness to compromised constituents is a property of the processes that allocate, audit and revise authority, not only of its constraints on harmful acts; safeguards against capture can also restrict the disagreement and revision that self-governance needs, and where they do security and self-governance trade off, while others, such as audits independent of the audited that protect dissent, serve both, so the two are distinct achievements and not opposed ones | The owner's question, U41 of the exchange of 2026-10-17: "is literature on organizational robustness to insider threats potentially useful to us?" It "integrates the Richens result rather than rejecting it, preserves [the] original critique of folk-model attributions, and connects both to the larger Nucleation program." Proposed: a definition and an organizing thesis, with the study [CASE-187](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-187.md) as its test. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-515](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-515.md) | Whether an organization has a cognitive property is four questions, not one: what information about the property can be recovered from its behaviour, what capabilities it can actually exercise, what mechanisms realize them, and whether it can maintain or transform those mechanisms; the four can come apart, and none should be silently substituted for another | The general principle the owner drew at the second review of the filing of the exchange "Analyze nucleation concepts" (2026-10-31): "When asking whether an organization 'has' a cognitive property, distinguish the information recoverable from its behavior, the capabilities it can actually exercise, the mechanisms realizing those capabilities, and its ability to maintain or transform those mechanisms." It was drawn from the world-model case ([CLAIM-514](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-514.md)) and judged "sufficiently general—and sufficiently testable—that it deserves an explicit place in Nucleation's research program". Proposed and interpretive: its instances are demonstrated case by case, and the generalization is not. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-519](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-519.md) v2 | Competent behaviour does not establish an internal world model: over a fixed interface and a finite horizon, an agent with no model, whose actions are looked up from the history so far, reproduces the interaction distribution of an agent that has one exactly; a policy can identify predictive structure without any particular internal component realizing it, so compression and generalization support comparing candidate architectures, and establishing an internal mechanism needs evidence that discriminates candidate implementations, such as targeted interventions | The owner's thesis at U20 of the exchange "Analyze nucleation concepts" (2026-10-31): that under the record's framework a world model is "essentially a 'folk' explanatory tool and that no such thing need explicitly be present for the external behavior to be indistinguishable from a comparable black box agent which actually did contain a world model". A20 agreed and gave the construction, with a limit the claim keeps: the attribution "sometimes ... names a genuine, interventionally identifiable computational mechanism". The construction is Block's lookup-table argument ([THEORY-092](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-092.md)) applied to agency, so it is elementary; the thesis is the reading of it. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-523](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-523.md) | For a normatively relevant discrepancy to change what an organization does, three distinct achievements are needed and any can fail while the others hold: legibility, by which the discrepancy becomes recognizable; volitional efficacy, by which a corresponding demand can move action; and correctability, by which a fitting revision can be carried out within deadline and resources; none establishes that the demand or the revision is justified, and whether the norm-satisfying histories the agent can still realize are empty depends partly on what its earlier actions destroyed | The owner's synthesis at review of the filing of the exchange "Analyze nucleation concepts" (2026-10-31). It was first filed as a dated note on [QUESTION-364](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-364.md), and filed as a claim at the owner's word ("this should probably be a new CLAIM, not hidden inside the prose of a QUESTION"). It joins three held entries, legibility ([TERM-064](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-064.md)), will-organization ([TERM-023](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-023.md)) and correctability ([TERM-085](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-085.md)), into one account of normative efficacy. It extends [CLAIM-349](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-349.md)'s split of access, authority and action from an organization's own signals to normatively relevant discrepancies. Proposed: the separations are argued, not built. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-527](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-527.md) | Viable reach, valence and emotion are three quantities in an organization, not one: an emotion is a claim to precedence, system valence is movement along the ordering that wins the negotiation, and a change in what the organization can viably reach is neither, so an organization can run ahead along its prevailing ordering while its viable reach contracts | Filed 2026-10-31 from the readings of Massumi and McKim (2009) and Bencherki, Brummans and Vézy (2024). Massumi's affect is a transition in a body's capacitation, augmented or diminished, and the parent paper defines agency as its augmenting half. The record's affect line reads emotion as a claim to precedence (Frijda) and system valence as movement along what wins the negotiation; neither is a change in what can be done. This claim names the third quantity, viable reach, and says it can move against valence. It does not say that Massumi's capacitation is viable reach, or that more reach is better. | Proposed |
